access_evidence: PROBES.json reg_mdall_001/002/003: HTTP 200 JSON for company search (6,909 bytes), licence search (55,291 bytes) and device search (45,068 bytes). The historical path /api/medical-device/device/ returns HTTP 404 (recorded in DATASETS/regulatory/_discovery/round1.json); the working base is /api/medical-devices/.
blockers: licence?company_id=N is unbounded for large firms (read timeout observed on Medtronic company_id 114663).
device?licence_number=N is documented but unscoped: every call returned >2.5 MB.
historical_depth: Two states: active (no cancellation date) and archived (carries end_date), so cancelled licences are retained. Per-device and per-identifier first/end dates are published. There is NO publication clock and NO status-change date.
licence_note: Open Government Portal dataset c801a084-210b-4cd2-8513-26a00b66eb6f 'Medical Devices Active Licence Listing (MDALL)' states licence_title 'Open Government Licence - Canada' with license_url https://open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada.
machine_interface: REST JSON/XML under https://health-products.canada.ca/api/medical-devices/: licence/, company/, device/, deviceidentifier/, licencetype/, sbdlocation/. Params: id, state (active|archived), licence_name, company_id, device_name, licence_number, device_identifier, lang, type.
name: Medical Devices Active Licence Listing (MDALL)
notes: Work-around used instead of the two broken filters: discover licences via licence_name=<keyword> and attribute them to a firm by the official company_id from company?company_name=<firm>; collect devices via device_name=<keyword>&state=active and attribute via original_licence_no. Documented in DATASETS/regulatory/canada_mdall/COUNTS.json.
rate_policy: No documented quota. Observed ~20 calls at ~1.2 req/s; the unbounded licence?company_id= and device?licence_number= calls time out or return >2.5 MB for large firms.
robots_summary: HTTP 404 (ASP.NET error page) — no robots policy is served.
what_is_new: First Canadian counterpart data in MedRadar with official licence numbers (original_licence_no) and per-identifier model tokens, which is what makes an FDA<->Canada identity experiment possible at all — and what exposes that the two jurisdictions share no identifier namespace.
